title: Release servo calibration scratch
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for the next model flip / runtime tweak. Not official runbook — laundry list + thoughts I want to remember while pairing with SRE.

Context:
- Target change: small kernel selection tweak + kv-cache limit adjustment to improve p95 in 16k-seq paths.
- Why this is risky: kernel path touches hot loops, untested on mixed-tenant traffic.
- Goal: validate no client-visible regressions and confirm cost/token impact for 24h.

Fast checklist (pre-traffic) — warmup these before any routing changes:
- [ ] Build image tagged: docker-serve:servo-cal-20260305 (confirm digest)
- [ ] Smoke-local: run perf harness vs baseline for 1h (seq=512, 2048, 16384) -> collect p50/p95/cpu/gpu-mem
- [ ] Canary config: feature-flag = feature/servo-cal-enable; route by API key cohort
- [ ] Add ephemeral metric hooks: model.latency.kvpath, kernel.codepath, cache.hits
- [ ] Alert thresholds pre-populated in temp channel (#deploys-kc)

Traffic plan (cohorts):
- T0 (5m): 0.5% traffic -> single region, single client-type (internal test account)
- T1 (30m): 2% traffic -> add 2 low-traffic customers, stagger by 10m
- T2 (1h): 10% traffic -> broad low-latency cohort, observe 2h
- T3 (2h): 30% traffic -> add warm clients, keep canary for 24h
- T4: full -> after 24h green

Quick ramp script (notes):
- curl -H "X-Test-Cohort:servo-t0" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate ... (wrap with load gen)
- use blue-green tag + rollout: `rbctl route set --cohort servo-cal --fraction 0.005`

Signals to watch (hard stop):
- p95 increase > 20% for more than 10m (across any cohort)
- error rate spike > 0.25% absolute from baseline for 5 consecutive minutes
- GPU OOM or eviction on any node
- Token cost delta > +15% (unexpected)
- Quality regression on golden prompt set: BLEU/ROUGE drop > 3 points or hallucination increase (manual checks)

Soft signals (pause & investigate):
- slow warmup of kv-cache (cache fills slower than baseline by >30m)
- slight p50 increases but stable p95
- small GC churn on host

Rollback play (fast):
- `rbctl route set --cohort servo-cal --fraction 0` (immediate stop)
- pin clients back to previous image with `image: docker-serve:baseline-20260210`
- open postmortem stub in JIRA (INFR-721) with initial timeline

Post-acceptance checks (if green):
- Keep canary for minimum 24h with increased telemetry retention for the cohort
- Run daily regression evals (subset of golden prompts + user-reported fuzz tests)
- Quantify cost delta (tokens / GPU-hours) across 24h windows vs same weekday baseline
- Schedule 1:1 with kernel lead (Ravi) to decide whether to roll to Dedicated pool

Open questions / decisions I still need to make:
- Should we enable prefix caching for this cohort earlier? Might hide the perf regressions. Recommendation: NO for first 2 phases.
- Metrics: do we need to split by client-sdk version? yes, add header-based split.
- Do we allow regional fallback auto-route during T1? Prefer manual for first 2 ramps.

Notes from the last smoke run (local):
- p95 improved by ~6% at seq=2048 but regressed by ~12% on 16k in worst case on VM with older cuda driver. Need to confirm infra baseline.
- KV cache hit-rate similar but eviction rate increased slightly; investigate allocator settings.

Quick commands / helpers (to copy):
- Add metric annotation: `metrics annotate --run servo-cal-20260305 --note "initial canary"`
- Shortcut to scale down cohort: `rbctl route set --cohort servo-cal --fraction 0`
- Health check: `kubectl get pods -l app=serve,env=servo-cal -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].restartCount}'`

Parking-lot (later follow-ups):
- automate gradual fractional increments using feedback loop (closed loop based on p95 target)
- add a canary-specific log sampler to collect traces only for servo-cal cohort (avoid noise)
- longer-term: add A/B eval harness so we can test quality delta in parallel with traffic

Random TODOs to not forget:
- ping infra to verify cuda driver matrix across staging and prod (Ravi)
- drop a note to CSM if we plan to include any external beta customers in T2
- update the rollout SOP with these kernel-specific watchlist items after this run

End of scratchpad. Will convert to a more formal runbook if we decide to promote.
